paper.title: LASER: LLM Agent with State-Space Exploration for Web Navigation
paper.central_claim: Model web navigation as transitions among predefined states with state-specific instructions/actions so an LLM can handle novel situations, easily backtrack from mistakes and always perform valid actions, outperform baselines without demonstrations, approach human live shopping performance, and generalize to other LLMs.

provenance.rubric_version: v2.2 draft_uncalibrated (supplied run snapshot; no independent freeze claim)
provenance.runtime_record_note: Model identity from invocation system context; no session/receipt identifier exposed; no model probing.

evidence.quote: This formulation enables flexible backtracking, allowing the model to recover from errors easily.
evidence.support_explanation: Central proposed causal benefit; broader than action-format validity.

evidence.quote: Experimental results show that LASER significantly outperforms previous methods and closes the gap with human performance on the web navigation task.
evidence.support_explanation: Original performance/general web claim must not silently be narrowed.

evidence.quote: After manually categorizing all possible states in the interactive task, for each state, we write a generic instruction that describes the state in detail.
evidence.support_explanation: Manual task-domain knowledge substitutes for oracle trajectories, not knowledge-free generality.

evidence.quote: At every step, the agent receives state-specific system instruction, current observation, a set of permissible actions in the current states, and the history of past thoughts and actions as inputs.
evidence.support_explanation: State-conditioned action/observation interface and episode history.

evidence.quote: We also define a memory buffer to store the intermediate results (the items examined but considered non-matching) during the exploration.
evidence.support_explanation: Episode-local backup candidates; not persistent cross-task experience learning.

evidence.quote: Success Rate Reward ASH Lo et al. (2023) 30.2 56.7 ReAct Yao et al. (2023) * 40.0 66.6 ReAct (ours rerun) 34.0 59.7 WebGUM Furuta et al. (2023) 45.0 67.5 LASER - backup 48.4 71.2 LASER 50.0 75.6
evidence.support_explanation: 500 live simulated episodes; matched GPT4 rerun controls backbone but not all prompts/interface differences.

evidence.quote: The standard LASER is powered by GPT-4 under zero-shot.
evidence.support_explanation: Zero-shot means no in-context trajectories, not no manual policy instruction.

evidence.quote: For the sim-to-real transfer experiments on amazon.com , we used the first 100 test set instructions from the WebShop.
evidence.support_explanation: Explicit 100 instruction denominator and instruction-source overlap across simulator/real site.

evidence.quote: we convert the webpages on amazon.com into the same format as the WebShop
evidence.support_explanation: Structured adapter shields raw live DOM variability; not screenshot-only grounding transfer.

evidence.quote: In particular, we manually annotated item attribute matches, item option matches, item category matches and item price matches.
evidence.support_explanation: Human result evaluation using WebShop reward functions; no inter-rater or blinded reliability study reported.

evidence.quote: We allow our agent to make 15 state transitions in maximum. In practice, if the agent has not reached the finish state after 13 state transitions, we force it to select from the history to ensure it does not exceed the budget.
evidence.support_explanation: Concrete hard cap and conditional final selection, but state transitions are not identical to LLM calls/tokens.

evidence.quote: Therefore we forced the agent to stop when it decides to buy the item when experimenting on amazon.com .
evidence.support_explanation: Real task is matching/choosing an item, not actual purchase or checkout execution.

evidence.quote: Due to the limited computing budget, we only ran our ablation studies on 200 instructions.
evidence.support_explanation: Ablation/test denominator differs from main500 and selection rule unspecified.

evidence.quote: We manually annotated 30 error cases from the Dev set
evidence.support_explanation: Not a census of test failures; 9 good-enough,12 retrieval,9 missing details.

evidence.quote: Our LASER requires manual annotation of possible states in the environment and their corresponding descriptions.
evidence.support_explanation: Applicability restricted to small known domain state spaces; annotation cost not quantified.

evidence.quote: Most similar to our work, Synapse
evidence.support_explanation: Authors acknowledge state-conditional prompting nearest neighbor; no independent original in fixed14-reference list.

evidence.quote: Success Rate Reward LASER 52.0 77.6 LASER + One-shot 50.0 74.9 LASER - function call 50.0 76.2 LASER (text-davinci-003) 38.5 70.2
evidence.support_explanation: Function calling contributes2pp on200 but does not isolate state abstraction/backtracking; no uncertainty.

evidence.quote: SR Reward Att. Opt. Type. LASER 62.0 85.4 85.5 75.0 97.0 Human Yao et al. (2022) 65.0 88.2 86.2 76.3 99.0
evidence.support_explanation: Live Amazon item-selection matches; human reference imported from prior work, not demonstrated contemporaneous paired evaluation.

evidence.quote: Since LASER already performs valid actions 100% time
evidence.support_explanation: Observed syntactic/action availability validity, not perfect correctness or a universal safety theorem.

evidence.quote: The results are shown in Table 3 . Again, the agent without function calling performs slightly worse on these 200 episodes.
evidence.support_explanation: Text JSON still provided permitted actions; removal does not test the state-specific action restrictions.

evidence.quote: If an item has been selected before (the button has been clicked), you should not select the same item again.
evidence.support_explanation: Explicit anti-repeat state instructions; history traces retained.

evidence.quote: Your task is to perform one of the function calls based on the rationale.
evidence.support_explanation: Thought generation and action selection split into two prompting steps. Cost must count both.

signatures.object: Shopping navigation policy and permissible actions
signatures.information: Structured text observation generated by WebShop/official Amazon-to-WebShop adapter, item/button labels, hand-labelled page state; no target gold item available to policy. Teacher demonstrations not used, but state/action knowledge manually supplied.
signatures.operation: Classify into search/results/item/finish by page layout -> state-specific instructions/layout -> GPT4 rationale -> second GPT4 function selection from state-specific actions -> execute -> update observation/history; back/prev enable revisiting prior states.
signatures.output: Search query, product selection, inspect description/features/reviews, navigate back/page forward, or Buy_Now terminal selection
signatures.conditions: Complete hand-enumerable small state space; correct adapter; reversible navigation; product information and search engine can expose target.
signatures.feedback: Actual next page after action, observed customization/details; semantic matching inferred by LLM, not privileged gold reward during action selection.
signatures.selection_rule: LLM picks one permitted function; no explicit candidate-tree optimizer or learned verifier.
signatures.selection_data: Current page, user instruction and episode thoughts/actions
signatures.persistence: Static prompts/state-action map across episodes; history only within episode; frozen backbone.
signatures.later_use: Next transition in same session; no accepted cross-task policy edits.
signatures.claimed_effect: Avoid invalid functions and recover from mistakes, increasing task success without demonstrations.
signatures.failure_boundary: Schema incompleteness or irreversible actions cannot be fixed just by Back; 100% observed validity != all actions correct; longer trajectories still degrade.

signatures.information: Only episode-observed item attributes, not gold matching score
signatures.operation: Store examined items in buffer -> at13 transitions request best past item -> finish by15 transitions
signatures.output: Fallback item if budget would expire
signatures.conditions: A useful candidate was visited, remembered and correctly selected; semantic error that rejected target initially must be overcome.
signatures.feedback: Page details and prior rationales, no external success-check feedback before selection
signatures.selection_rule: Forced LLM selection among history; no acceptance gate for persisted learning.
signatures.persistence: Episode-local buffer; no demonstrated carryover across tasks
signatures.failure_boundary: Conditioned difficult15-step group still poor; no task reuse or retention gain evidence.

retained_chain.reason: No self-improvement claim: prompts and backbone fixed, observed candidates retained only within episode. No cross-task accepted changes, parameter updates or later-task retained-gain test.

gap.author_gap: Forward-only oracle demonstrations omit error recovery; global action spaces allow impossible actions; covering every mistake with examples costly.
gap.checked_gap: Specific invalid Next-on-item-page example and repeated-next failures establish interface-level bottleneck; oracle demonstrations are not logically incapable of supporting recovery, so broad premise is not proven.

gap.method_response: Encode state-action topology and state prompts; rationale-to-function loop; finite-budget candidate backup.
gap.remaining_gap: No universal recovery guarantee, arbitrary-domain state discovery, real purchase safety or complete attribution of state abstraction itself.

Episode product buffer and no-backup comparison; no memory-driven step-savings measurement.

unassigned: Manual finite-state permitted-action routing is not fully distinguished by gui:C20; retained as operation detail rather than inventing a new frozen subcard.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: State-indexed instructions and allowed functions constrain each prompted reason/action loop; current page and history feed next transition.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions/differences: Only state/action-name admissibility encoded; C20 thought loop alone does not describe topology; no graph-message-passing, manager, learned reflector or irreversible rollback.
